blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Switchboard Upgrade Cost in Geelong?
blogPosts.excerpt: Find out what a switchboard upgrade costs in Geelong, why older homes in Lara and Geelong West need one, and what Australian safety standards require.
body: If you live in an older Geelong home, there is a good chance your switchboard has not been upgraded in decades. Many houses in suburbs like Lara, Geelong West, and East Geelong still have ceramic fuse boxes that predate modern safety switch technology. A switchboard upgrade is one of the most important electrical investments a Geelong homeowner can make, and understanding the costs involved helps you plan for this essential safety improvement.

In the Geelong region, a standard switchboard upgrade typically costs between $800 and $2,500 depending on the size of your property and the complexity of the existing wiring. For a standard three-bedroom home in Lara or Hamlyn Heights, you can expect to pay around $1,000 to $1,500 for a complete upgrade that includes RCD safety switches on every circuit. Larger Geelong properties or those with additional circuits such as air conditioning and solar systems will be at the higher end of this range.

The cost depends on several key factors specific to your Geelong property. The number of circuits in your home is the primary driver — a home with ten circuits will require more RCD protection than one with six. The condition of your existing wiring also matters significantly. If your Geelong home has older VIR (vulcanised Indian rubber) cabling, your electrician may recommend partial rewiring alongside the switchboard upgrade, which adds to the overall investment but is critical for safety.

Australian standards require that all new switchboard installations comply with AS/NZS 3000, commonly known as the Wiring Rules. This means every circuit must be protected by a safety switch rated at 30mA for personal protection. Many Geelong homes built before 2000 do not meet this standard, which means they are not compliant with current regulations. This becomes particularly important when selling your Geelong property, as buyers and their building inspectors will flag non-compliant switchboards immediately.

Geelong's coastal climate also plays a role in switchboard degradation. Properties closer to Corio Bay and the Surf Coast, including Lara and Point Henry, experience higher salt air exposure that can accelerate corrosion of electrical components. If your switchboard is externally mounted or located in a garage near the coast, the degradation can be faster than in more sheltered Geelong suburbs like Highton or Belmont. Regular inspections by a licensed Geelong electrician can catch these issues early.

Harris Electrixs has upgraded hundreds of switchboards across Geelong, Lara, and surrounding suburbs. We provide a fixed upfront quote before any work begins, and every upgrade includes a full compliance certificate. Our electricians assess your specific property, explain exactly what needs to be done, and complete the upgrade with minimal disruption to your home. Contact us today for a free switchboard assessment anywhere in the Geelong region.

blogPosts.title: Signs Your Geelong Home Needs a Complete Electrical Rewire
blogPosts.excerpt: Learn the warning signs that your older Geelong home may need a full rewire, from tripping breakers to outdated cabling types common in Lara and East Geelong.
body: Geelong has a rich mix of housing stock, from Federation-era homes in East Geelong and Newtown to mid-century properties in Lara and Corio. Many of these older homes still operate on original electrical wiring that was installed decades ago under very different safety standards. Knowing the warning signs that your Geelong home needs a complete rewire can prevent dangerous electrical faults, reduce your insurance risk, and bring your property up to current Australian standards.

The most common sign that a Geelong home needs rewiring is frequent circuit breaker tripping or fuse blowing. If you find that turning on the kettle while the dishwasher is running trips your switchboard, your wiring is likely unable to handle modern electrical loads. Geelong homes built before 1980 were designed for far fewer appliances than today's households use, and the original wiring gauge may be insufficient for your current power demands. This is especially common in older Lara and Norlane properties.

Another critical warning sign is the presence of outdated wiring types. Many pre-1970 Geelong homes contain VIR (vulcanised Indian rubber) cabling, which becomes brittle and dangerous with age. You may notice discoloured or cracked cable insulation in your roof space or switchboard. Aluminium wiring, common in some 1960s and 1970s Geelong constructions, also presents fire risks at connection points. A licensed Geelong electrician can identify these cable types during a safety inspection and advise whether a full or partial rewire is necessary.

Physical signs around your home can also indicate wiring problems. Flickering lights in your Geelong home, particularly when multiple appliances are running, suggest the wiring cannot handle the load. Warm or discoloured power point covers, a burning smell from switches, or tingling sensations when touching appliances are all serious red flags that require immediate attention from a qualified electrician. These symptoms are common in Geelong suburbs with older housing stock such as Geelong West and East Geelong.

The cost of rewiring a Geelong home varies significantly based on the size of the property and the complexity of the job. A full rewire of a standard three-bedroom house in Lara typically costs between $8,000 and $15,000, while larger Geelong homes or those with difficult access may cost more. While this is a significant investment, it brings your home fully up to current Australian standards, reduces fire risk substantially, and adds considerable value to your property. Many Geelong buyers now request electrical compliance certificates as part of their purchase due diligence.

Harris Electrixs has extensive experience rewiring homes across Geelong and Lara. We start with a comprehensive electrical assessment of your property, identify all areas of concern, and provide a detailed fixed-price quote for the rewire. Our team works efficiently to minimise disruption, and we coordinate with your sparkie and builder if other renovation work is happening simultaneously. Contact Harris Electrixs today for a thorough electrical inspection of your older Geelong home.

blogPosts.title: Energy-Efficient Lighting Upgrades for Geelong Homes and Businesses
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover how LED lighting upgrades can slash your Geelong power bills, improve safety, and meet Australian energy efficiency standards for residential and commercial properties.
body: Geelong homeowners and businesses are increasingly switching to energy-efficient LED lighting to reduce power costs and improve the quality of their indoor and outdoor spaces. With electricity prices continuing to rise across Victoria, upgrading your lighting is one of the fastest and most cost-effective ways to cut your energy consumption. A licensed Geelong electrician from Harris Electrixs can assess your current lighting setup and recommend LED solutions tailored to your property and budget.

The energy savings from switching to LED lighting in a typical Geelong home are substantial. A single 10W LED globe produces the same light output as an old 60W incandescent bulb while using just a fraction of the electricity. For a Geelong household running 30 light fittings, switching to LEDs can save over $400 per year on electricity bills. Commercial properties in Geelong CBD, Belmont, and Highton see even greater savings given the higher usage hours, with some businesses reporting reductions of 60 to 70 percent in lighting energy costs.

Beyond pure cost savings, LED lighting offers significant advantages for Geelong homes. Modern LED fittings produce a cleaner, more natural light that improves visibility and reduces eye strain compared to older halogen downlights, which are still common in many Geelong properties. LED fittings also produce significantly less heat, which is an important consideration for ceiling installations in Geelong homes where halogen downlights have historically been a fire risk near insulation. Replacing halogens with LEDs is one of the most impactful safety upgrades you can make.

For Geelong businesses, proper lighting directly impacts productivity, customer experience, and workplace safety. Retail shops in Geelong CBD and Belmont benefit from LED display lighting that renders colours more accurately, while offices in Highton and Waurn Ponds see improved staff wellbeing with well-designed LED panel installations. Harris Electrixs works with Geelong businesses of all sizes to design and install commercial lighting systems that balance energy efficiency with functional performance.

The Victorian Government offers various rebates and incentives for energy-efficient lighting upgrades, and Geelong businesses may qualify for additional support through regional development programs. A qualified Geelong electrician can help you navigate these incentives and ensure your lighting upgrade meets all eligibility requirements. The upfront investment in LED technology typically pays for itself within two to three years through reduced electricity consumption, making it one of the smartest investments for any Geelong property.

Harris Electrixs has completed LED lighting upgrades for hundreds of Geelong homes and businesses, from simple globe replacements to full commercial lighting fit-outs. We source high-quality Australian-compliant LED products and provide a complete service from assessment through to installation and testing. Whether you are in Lara, Belmont, Geelong West, or anywhere across the Geelong region, contact us today for a free lighting assessment and quote.

blogPosts.title: Electrical Safety Checks Every Geelong Landlord Must Complete
blogPosts.excerpt: A complete guide to mandatory electrical safety requirements for rental properties in Geelong, including smoke alarm compliance and switchboard standards.
body: Being a landlord in Geelong comes with significant electrical safety obligations under Victorian legislation. The Residential Tenancies Act and Electrical Safety Act require that all rental properties in Geelong meet strict electrical safety standards at the commencement of every tenancy. Failure to comply can result in substantial fines, voided insurance, and most importantly, serious safety risks to your tenants. Understanding these requirements is essential for every Geelong property investor.

Smoke alarm compliance is the most critical and well-known obligation for Geelong landlords. Victorian law requires that every rental property has interconnected smoke alarms in every bedroom, hallways connecting bedrooms, and on each level of the property. These alarms must be hardwired with battery backup or interconnected photoelectric alarms that meet Australian Standard AS 3786. For older Geelong rental properties in suburbs like Lara, Corio, and East Geelong, upgrading from standalone alarms to interconnected systems is often necessary to achieve full compliance.

Beyond smoke alarms, Geelong landlords must ensure that the entire electrical installation in their rental property is safe and compliant. This includes a current switchboard with RCD safety switches protecting all circuits, safe and functional power points and light fittings, and no exposed or damaged wiring. Victoria's rental safety regulations now require that a qualified electrician conducts an electrical safety check and provides a compliance certificate. This inspection must be completed before a new tenancy begins and at regular intervals thereafter.

The cost of electrical safety compliance for a Geelong rental property is modest compared to the potential consequences of non-compliance. A comprehensive electrical safety inspection by a licensed Geelong electrician typically costs between $150 and $300, with any required remedial work quoted separately. Common issues found in older Geelong rental properties include missing RCD protection, deteriorated wiring, damaged power points, and non-compliant smoke alarm installations. Addressing these promptly protects your investment and your tenants.

Geelong's property management companies increasingly require landlords to provide current electrical compliance documentation as part of their management agreements. Properties in high-demand rental suburbs like Belmont, Highton, and Geelong West must meet these standards to attract quality tenants who are aware of their rights. A property with current electrical compliance certificates also commands better rental returns and is easier to sell when the time comes, as buyers and their conveyancers routinely request this documentation.

We conduct thorough assessments of your rental property, issue compliance certificates, and complete any remedial work required to bring your installation up to current standards. Our team works efficiently to minimise vacancy periods and coordinates directly with your property manager if needed. Contact Harris Electrixs today to schedule your Geelong rental property electrical safety check.
